section_summary.extract_value: The discussion reports that a one-dimensional Standard Chinese translation of the BAS-2 showed adequate fit, good internal consistency, and convergent validity; body appreciation correlated with life satisfaction and self-esteem and—specifically in women—with weight discrepancy and BMI. The BAS-2 factor structure was invariant across sex, no significant overall sex difference in BAS-2 scores was found, and Standard Chinese respondents had slightly higher (negligible effect) body appreciation than Cantonese respondents; the section calls for replication in other Standard Chinese samples and additional validity evidence.
section_summary.evidence_source: 'Using CFA, we found that the one-dimensional model...had adequate fit in respondents who completed a Standard Chinese translation of the BAS-2.'; 'Specifically, we found that body appreciation scores were significantly associated with life satisfaction and self-esteem, and, in women only, with weight discrepancy and BMI.'; 'Our CFA results also showed that the one-dimensional model of body appreciation was invariant across sex.'

section_summary.extract_value: The section reports that a one-dimensional model of the Standard Chinese BAS-2 demonstrated adequate fit, internal consistency, and convergent validity. Measurement invariance across sex was supported, and no significant overall difference in BAS-2 scores between women and men was found, though associations with BMI were observed in women only. The authors compare Standard Chinese and Cantonese respondents and note limitations and directions for future validation work.
section_summary.evidence_source: 'Using CFA, we found that the one-dimensional model, in which all items loaded onto a single factor, had adequate fit in respondents who completed a Standard Chinese translation of the BAS-2.'; 'Our CFA results also showed that the one-dimensional model of body appreciation was invariant across sex. We found no significant difference in body appreciation scores between women and men.'

section_summary.extract_value: The Discussion reports that confirmatory factor analysis supported a one-dimensional factor structure for the Standard Chinese version of the BAS-2 and that this version demonstrated good internal consistency and convergent validity. The factor structure was invariant across sex, there was no significant difference in BAS-2 scores between women and men, and body appreciation was significantly associated with life satisfaction and self-esteem, and with BMI and weight discrepancy in women only; the section also compares Standard Chinese and Cantonese respondent groups (Standard Chinese scores were slightly higher but with a negligible effect size).
section_summary.evidence_source: "Using CFA, we found that the one-dimensional model, in which all items loaded onto a single factor, had adequate fit in respondents who completed a Standard Chinese translation of the BAS-2." "...scores on the Standard Chinese version of the BAS-2 have good internal consistency and convergent validity." "Specifically, we found that body appreciation scores were significantly associated with life satisfaction and self-esteem, and, in women only, with weight discrepancy and BMI." "Results showed that the latter had significantly higher body appreciation, although the effect size of this difference was negligible."
